ai.thread_title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: pricing confirmed, early use cases emerge
ai.name: OpenAI / Claire Vo, Dan Shipper, Swyx
ai.hook: Astra $8/MTok (20% cheaper); excels at animation, hard to steer. Sol as reliable workhorse.
insights: **$8/MTok** input pricing (20% cheaper than 6 Astra)
**Animation and pixel-level code generation** are Astra's strengths
**Steering/behavior remains difficult** per early user reports
Efficiency gains real; marketing was tone-deaf per Swyx
ai.for_you: Test Astra this week on animation or creative code tasks for PT SMB clients (e-commerce, gaming). Use Fable 5.2 for precision/compliance work. Astra is speed+creativity, not accuracy.
ai.what_changed: Pricing confirmed today. Early users publishing real examples (interactive storybooks, 3D animation). Dan Shipper live-testing against competitors today.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Pricing and use cases now clear and directly actionable for model selection.

ai.thread_title: Apple adds more permission alerts for agents; friction worsens
ai.name: Peter Steinberger
ai.hook: Instead of fixing agent permissions, Apple added scarier alerts. Friction is architectural.
insights: Developers asked Apple to **reduce permission prompts**
Apple's answer: **add more, scarier alerts** instead
Problem is **not solvable by UI design**; it's fundamental to OS model
ai.for_you: If you deploy agents to clients' Macs for local work, expect constant user interruption and permission denials. This may force you toward cloud-based or browser-based agent architecture instead. Plan around this constraint.
ai.what_changed: Peter Steinberger confirms latest Apple update worsens, not improves, the permission friction signal.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Real architectural constraint affecting agent deployment strategy.

ai.thread_title: Safe code execution for agents: isolation patterns prevent host damage
ai.name: Simon Willison, Prime Radiant
ai.hook: Run agents safely in isolated sandboxes; zero damage risk even on prompt injection attack.
insights: **Three sandbox models**: WebAssembly (browser), QEMU (virtual machine), Apple Container
Agents run on your machine but **execute in isolated environment**
Demo code with **working examples for Claude Code, Codex, Pi** published
ai.for_you: If you deploy agents for code or systems work with PT SMB clients, use external sandboxes to cut liability risk. Test WebAssembly approach this week if building browser-based tools.
ai.what_changed: Simon Willison published detailed blog post and GitHub examples; now has authoritative patterns for three sandbox types.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Practical safety pattern; reduces risk and liability for agent deployments.
